title: ONI Companion Link: companion/commands/cmd-<seq>.json (v1.3)
description: Written by the core (write-tmp-then-rename) into <ONI user folder>/companion/commands/. The mod picks it up with a FileSystemWatcher, runs it on the main thread, writes companion/acks/ack-<seq>.json, then deletes the command file. ALLOW LIST (v1.3): `focus`, `art_request`, `alert_activate`, `alert_dismiss`, `set_speed`, `sync_assets`, `overlay_set`, `tool_select`, `build_select`; anything else is logged and dropped. The mod ignores a command whose createdAt is older than 10 s, runs at most 1 focus per 250 ms (art_request only queues, one per frame), and never acts on paths or code from a command. alert_activate = do what a click on that live alert, or on one of its highlighted lines (`link` = AlertLink.index), does in the game, through the game's own click path (so focus cycles like the game does); one camera move or one screen open, never a follow. alert_dismiss = dismiss that alert exactly as the game does, and only when the alert is dismissable; otherwise failed with "Can't be dismissed". Unknown alertId = failed "Alert is gone". set_speed = pause, or play at `speed` (default: the speed the game had), or speed = select `speed` and keep the pause state (the game's speed buttons), through the game's own speed control; the mod writes live.json at once afterwards. sync_assets = draw the catalog (`full`: everything, `missing`: only what the art manifest lacks or whose srcKey changed), export the Graystroke atlas + glyph table and the theme; the mod pauses the game while it runs and restores the previous speed after, writes companion/sync/status.json (mod-sync-status.schema.json), and acks at once (done "Started", or failed "Already running" / "No colony loaded" if it needs one). focus = ONE move of the camera (never the game's follow mode). art_request = draw one catalog image on demand: target.kind is a catalog art kind (never dupe: portraits draw themselves), target.id the game's id (letters, digits, _ . -, at most 100). The ack comes after the art manifest lists the image (done), or at once with the reason (failed, e.g. "Unknown id"). v1.3: overlay_set = switch the game to the overlay `mode` (an export overlays[].id) through the game's own overlay path; the active overlay again, or mode "None", goes back to no overlay like the game; failed with the reason for an unknown or unavailable mode ("Not available in this game"). tool_select = activate the tool `tool` (an export tools[].id) in the game, ready to drag on the game screen; `priority` (1..9 or "emergency") sets the game's priority first like its priority bar; with `priority` and no `tool` only the priority changes; failed for an unknown tool or one the game does not offer. build_select = open the game's build menu on `buildingId` and pick it for placement as if the player had clicked it; `materials` are element ids, one per material slot in the building's order, picked in the game's own material selector; `facadeId` picks a facade. failed with the game's reason: "Not researched yet" (add the tech name when the mod knows it), "Not available in this game", "Not enough <material>" (the game keeps its own choice for that slot). Same limits and acks as every command; the mod never acts on paths or code from a command.

mode.description: An export overlays[].id, or None for no overlay.

priority.description: The game's priority setting: 1..9 or the string emergency.

materials.description: Element id per material slot, in the building's slot order.

seq.description: Set by the core; the ack file uses the same number.

select.description: Also select the target so its info panel opens. Default true.

link.description: AlertLink.index; absent = the alert's main click.

speed.description: Optional with state play (absent = keep the game's selected speed); required with state speed.
